question: In Jainism, the word 'Jain' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jina', which means,______ implying one who has transcended all human passions.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Conqueror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'Jain' is derived from the Sanskrit word **'Jina', meaning conqueror**, signifying one who has overcome inner enemies like desire, anger, pride, and greed.
 
• In Jainism, a 'Jina' is a spiritual victor who has achieved liberation (moksha) by conquering all worldly attachments and passions.
 
• A 'Jina' is also referred to as a **Tirthankara**, a teacher who establishes the path to liberation for others.
 
• Jainism emphasizes non-violence (ahimsa), truth (satya), and self-discipline as key virtues that help individuals become spiritual conquerors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tirthankaras:** Jainism recognizes 24 Tirthankaras, with Lord Mahavira being the 24th and most recent one. Tirthankaras are spiritual leaders who guide others towards liberation.
 
• **Moksha:** Liberation or salvation in Jainism is achieved by freeing oneself from the cycle of birth and rebirth (samsara) through the conquest of all passions and desires.
 
• **Ahimsa (Non-violence):** A core principle of Jainism, emphasizing absolute non-violence in thought, word, and action towards all living beings.
 
• **Core Teachings of Jainism:** The three main pillars are Right Faith (Samyak Darshana), Right Knowledge (Samyak Jnana), and Right Conduct (Samyak Charitra).
 
• **Jain Literature:** Jain texts such as the Agamas and Tattvartha Sutra provide detailed teachings on how to live a virtuous life and attain liberation.
